newsitem.title: CUBA: Saddam Hussein holds talks with Cuban envoy.
newsitem.headline: Saddam Hussein holds talks with Cuban envoy.

text.p: A Cuban envoy expressing his nation's condemnation of U.S. attacks on Iraq has met President Saddam Hussein in Baghdad, the Cuban news agency, Prensa Latina, said on Friday.

Quoting a statement from the Cuban Embassy in the Iraqi capital, the news agency said Rodrigo Alvarez Cambras, who heads the Cuba-Iraq Friendship Association, had discussed "common interests" with Saddam.

Alvarez Cambras, a member of the Central Committee of Cuba's ruling Communist Party, told the Iraqi president the Cuban government considered last week's U.S. missile attacks on Iraq as "a gross violation of sovereignty and international norms and treaties."

He and Saddam also discussed Cuban-Iraqi relations in such areas as trade and industrial and health cooperation, Prensa Latina said, citing the embassy statement. It did not specify when the meeting took place.
The Cuban, who frequently acts as a kind of roving ambassador in the Middle East region, arrived in Baghdad early last week.
At the time the 1991 Gulf War, Cuba criticised the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait but then strongly condemned the subsequent U.S.-led military campaign against Iraq.
